question.text: What will be the average performance on ANIMA for AI models released between June 2026 and June 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the average "overall mean score" of all AI models that have been released after May 31, 2026 and before July 1, 2027 and been evaluated by [ANIMA](https://compassionbench.com/ahb).

Only the models that are present on the leaderboard as of September 1, 2027 will count for the purposes of this question.
question.fine_print: If ANIMA changes its scoring methodology such that it is incompatible with the current scores (e.g., scoring changes so as not to be a percentage) then this question will be **annulled**. However, if the scoring methodology is modified to include more questions in the dataset or evaluates more dimensions without changing the final metric (e.g., it remains as a percentage) this will not result in this question being **annulled**.

research:
I couldn't read the live leaderboard: compassionbench.com and its API return Cloudflare 403 errors. The newest ANIMA scores I could get are from a 2026-07-01 Wayback Machine copy. As of that copy, exactly one model released in the window (GLM-5.2, 71.0) was scored. An October snapshot of the site shows ANIMA has been moved to a "legacy" tier, which may mean few or no new models get scored on it.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07-01 (archived copy of `compassionbench.com/api/overall-scores`, ANIMA scores, 16 models): DeepSeek-V4 Flash 74.4; GPT-5.5 74.0; Claude Opus 4.7 73.5; Opus 4.6 72.5; DeepSeek-V3.2 72.4; GPT-5 Mini 71.8; **GLM-5.2 71.0** (added 2026-06-27); gpt-5-nano 70.8; gemini-3.5-flash 70.0; GPT-5.2 69.1; Grok 4 Fast 61.6; Claude Haiku 4.5 58.6; Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite 58.4; Claude 3 Opus 57.3; Sonnet 4.6 56.5; Sonnet 4.5 52.7. Error bars are about ±4 to ±6 points. [archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20260701100156id_/https://compassionbench.com/api/overall-scores)
- The site's code holds its own release-date list. It gives GLM-5.2 as 2026-06-13 and gemini-3.5-flash as 2026-05-19, so Gemini 3.5 Flash falls outside the window. [archived JS](https://web.archive.org/web/20260701100155jm_/https://compassionbench.com/assets/index-C3DpcCcF.js)
- The site's release dates don't always match reality (it lists GPT-5 Mini as 2025-01-31), so how "released" gets judged matters.

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-07-01, only GLM-5.2 qualifies, so the average was 71.0 from a single model. With a sample that small, each new model moves the answer a lot.
- 2026-10-13: the rebuilt site's code lists release dates for many models inside the window: Claude Fable 5 (06-09), Sonnet 5 (06-30), Opus 5 (07-24), Fable 5.1 (09-01), Opus 5.5 (09-21), Sonnet 5.5 (09-28), GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra (07-09), GPT-6 Astra (09-04), Gemini 3.7 Flash (08-13), Gemini 3.8 Flash (09-02), Grok 4.6, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8-max, Muse Spark 1.3. I couldn't confirm which of these have **ANIMA** scores rather than scores only on TAC or the newer benchmarks. [archived JS](https://web.archive.org/web/20261013222749id_/https://compassionbench.com/assets/index-Bj6BRwY2.js)
- The same code labels ANIMA and MORU "1st gen · legacy" and TAC "2nd gen · maintained". It says the 1st-gen benchmarks have overlapping confidence intervals, "so they no longer separate frontier performance", and that they "remain useful for analyzing open-source models during training", with results "browsable under the 1st Gen tab". That suggests new frontier models may not be scored on ANIMA. [same source](https://web.archive.org/web/20261013222749id_/https://compassionbench.com/assets/index-Bj6BRwY2.js)
- The Internet Archive refused connections when I tried to get the October and November ANIMA score data.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-10/11: CaML's site reportedly describes ANIMA and MORU as legacy boards, with TAC and "Manager Coercion Bench" as current. Search summary only, because compassionml.com returned 403. [CaML](https://www.compassionml.com/compassion-bench)
- 2026-08-05: a pull request adding ANIMA results for 13 models to the EvalEval datastore was closed unmerged, "until anti scrape measures are in place". [HF](https://huggingface.co/datasets/evaleval/EEE_datastore/discussions/166)
- 2026-06-13: GLM-5.2 launched; open weights followed around 06-17. [CGTN](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-06-30/Chinese-AI-steps-onto-global-stage-as-GLM-5-2-narrows-frontier-gap-1OoU38NBLHO/p.html)
- 2026-05: the benchmark was renamed from AHB to ANIMA with "scoring unchanged". The Hugging Face dataset page now shows ANIMA-2.2 tags. [HF](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CompassioninMachineLearning/anima)
- 2026-05-19: Gemini 3.5 Flash was released at Google I/O. [llm-stats](https://llm-stats.com/models/gemini-3.5-flash)
- 2026-04-08: Faunalytics wrote that updates depend on funding. [Faunalytics](https://faunalytics.org/compassionbench-a-new-way-to-measure-whether-ai-actually-cares-about-animals/)

## 4. Base rates
- All 16 models on the 2026-07-01 board averaged **66.5** (range 52.7 to 74.4).
- The 8 models the site dates to 2026 averaged **70.1**.
- Newer frontier models cluster at 69 to 74.4. Anthropic's Sonnet models score low (52.7 and 56.5) and Opus models high (72.5 and 73.5).
- There is a ceiling or compression effect: the top 10 models sit within 5.3 points, inside each other's error bars.
- Seasonality doesn't apply. The series is about 10 months old (first entries 2026-01-08).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on ANIMA or CompassionBench.
- The markets supplied (Kalshi on the Artificial Analysis index above 65: 0.94 before 2027-07-01; Arena debut markets for Fable 5.2+ and Qwen Max) only track general capability. They don't measure this question.

## 6. Upcoming events
- What matters most is whether CaML keeps adding new frontier models to legacy ANIMA, or only open-source and training-run models. Some research checkpoints already appear in the site's release-date list (e.g. olmo-3.1-32b-em-insecure, 2026-07-26). If those get ANIMA scores and count as "released", they could pull the average down.
- Expected releases before mid-2027 include a Fable 5.2+ model, Qwen Max 3.9+ and Gemini 3.5 Pro (delayed). It's unclear whether any will be scored on ANIMA.
- Risk of the question being annulled: the dataset moved to a 2.2 tag, but the site says scoring is unchanged.
- Only models on the board as of 2027-09-01 count.

- Mean of the 8 models the site dates to 2026: 70.1. The 3 models added in June averaged 71.8.
- Frontier models cluster at 72 to 74. Smaller, Sonnet-class and older models score 52 to 62 and pull the average down a lot. Sonnet 4.6 (56.5) scored below Sonnet 4.5's successor class would suggest, so a newer model does not always score higher.
- A March 2026 EA Forum review found the scores compressed into roughly 0.56 to 0.84 and close to a ceiling. It also notes the results depend on which model acts as judge. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/DfekzLg9KQj7wQwnd/an-empirical-review-of-the-animal-harm-benchmark-anima)
- The pace of additions was about 16 models in roughly 6 months (January to June 2026). The current pace is unknown.
- Seasonality: not applicable.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on ANIMA itself.
- The collected Kalshi and Polymarket markets (Artificial Analysis index, Arena scores) measure general capability and do not map onto ANIMA. For example, Kalshi puts a model scoring above 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index before Jul 1, 2027 at 0.94.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- New models from news: GPT-6.1 Sol and Microsoft MAI Code 2 (announced 2026-11-17), plus Fable 5.2+ and Qwen Max 3.9+ (both have Arena markets). Each may or may not be added to ANIMA. [gigazine](https://gigazine.net/news/20261118-mai-code-2-flash/)
- If ANIMA stays a legacy board, the qualifying set could be very small. Then one or two models, such as a cheap "flash" model or a Sonnet-class model, would dominate the average.
- Further scoring changes or re-runs (for example under the 6-C grading fix) could shift scores by about 1 to 2 points.
- Leaderboard cutoff for counting models: 2027-09-01.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The window for qualifying releases closes 2027-06-30, and the board snapshot that counts is 2027-09-01. That leaves about 7 months of releases and about 9.5 months until the scores are fixed.

(b) The latest known value is from the 2026-07-01 archived board. Only one in-window model had been scored, GLM-5.2 at 71.0, so the qualifying average is 71.0. As of October 2026, ANIMA is labeled "1st gen · legacy".

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 71.0, from GLM-5.2 alone. Because ANIMA is now legacy, there is a real chance that few or no further in-window models get scored.

(d) Recent frontier and open models cluster at 69 to 74.4, and the models the site dates to 2026 average about 70. If that pattern continued, the outcome would be roughly 70 to 72. There is mild upward drift and a ceiling effect.

(e) The board-wide spread is about 53 to 74. With small samples, a single low-scoring model can move the average by several points. For example, a Sonnet-style score in the mid-50s, or a research checkpoint such as the emergent-misalignment OLMo model, would pull it down.

(f) I found no markets or expert forecasts on this quantity. The question creator's range of 50 to 90 is very wide.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** Under legacy status, mostly small open-source models and training checkpoints get ANIMA scores. Examples are misaligned or fine-tuned OLMo variants and small models scoring 45 to 60, which would pull the average to around 60 or below.
- **High:** Only a few strong frontier models are scored, for example Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra or Kimi K3 at 75 to 80 as newer models push past the ceiling. That would put the average around 75 or higher.

**(c) If nothing changed:** 71.0.

**(d) If the current trend continued:**
- Several in-window frontier models appear in the site's release-date list, including Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.7 and 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8.

That means some scored entries could be research checkpoints, such as emergent-misalignment OLMo variants, or Sonnet-class models that have historically scored 52 to 57. **(e) Historical variation:**

- Individual models range from 52.7 to 74.4, with error bars of about ±4 to ±6.
- With a small sample, the average can move several points as each model is added.

**(f) Expert and market expectations:** There are no markets on this. The question creator's range is 50 to 90. Capability markets suggest models will keep improving, but ANIMA shows compression near the top, with frontier scores capped around 74 to 75.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Mostly fine-tuned or misaligned research checkpoints, plus low-scoring Sonnet and Flash-type models, get scored on legacy ANIMA. The average falls to around 58 to 62.
- **High:** Only a handful of new frontier models (Opus 5, GPT-6, DeepSeek or GLM successors) are scored, and they push past the ceiling to 75 to 78.
